body:
Codex round 2: ACCEPT pushbacks A and B, with candidate provenance and late-chunking ablations added to the ADR. I inspected grakern and graph4s rather than guessing. Findings and final conditions:

1. Dependency boundary. grakern-core is lightweight and portable, but grakern-standard currently depends on grakern-graph4s, which in turn pulls graph4s core, indexed, and data on all three platforms. The WL compiler and query overlay are currently in engine-jvm. Therefore graph4s is technically cross-platform, but importing grakern-standard into embed-core would make a substantial topology stack part of the portable public footprint. I object to that.

2. Dogfood without leakage. Add an optional embed-grakern adapter module. Its internal adapter may depend on PropositionChart plus grakern-standard and graph4s, but no graph4s or grakern type appears in embed-core, narrative APIs, FeatureSpace identity, or serialized StoryModel contracts. Better upstream direction: move a minimal topology-neutral labelled-neighbourhood or graph-sample protocol and the WL feature compiler into portable grakern modules; keep graph4s as one adapter. That still dogfoods grakern while avoiding graph4s as a storymodel ontology dependency.

3. M1 portability claim. Until the WL compiler leaves engine-jvm, the grakern structural provider is JVM-only. Do not advertise it as the portable free tier merely because grakern core and standard cross-build. Either land and gate the upstream portability bead first, or label the M1 adapter JVM-only. No hidden in-tree replacement under the same provider ID.

4. Directedness is a real upstream blocker. Current WLTrace builds an incident neighbourhood and uses the same edge key from both endpoints. A role label alone therefore does not guarantee that ARG0 source-to-target differs from the reversed relation. The grakern law must show that reversing a directed proposition edge changes the structural features or kernel, while alpha-renaming and edge enumeration order do not. Orientation needs to be relative to the incident endpoint, not just embedded once in an undirected edge label.

5. Query overlay. grakern already has WLQueryTrace and WLQueryAlignment in engine-jvm, so the bead is verify, harden, and benchmark rather than invent. Required evidence: prepared source state remains immutable; query-only colours do not contaminate the source dictionary; batch cost scales with query graph size plus sparse output rather than rebuilding the source Gram; exact cross values match full recompilation on small oracles.

6. Pinning. storymodel4s may pin grakern by immutable SHA and grakern may pin graph4s by immutable SHA, with local build overrides only for development. Both transitive SHAs belong in the build receipt. The release path must prove a clean clone without sibling checkouts. Replace ProjectRef pins with published artifacts once grakern 0.1 and graph4s releases exist.

7. Keep estimands separate. Structural grakern output belongs in structural.* and d_prop; dense language-model geometry belongs in semantic.* and d_sem. They can both nominate candidates, but a fused rank does not erase their identities. The feature-use ledger records which channels nominated each candidate and which entered any boundary induction.

8. Late chunking acceptance. A late-pooled view is a distinct FeatureSpace, not a silent fallback to template context. Its receipt must include tokenizer offsets, model context limit, window and stride policy, overlap merge, pooling rule, uncovered support, and Matryoshka dimension. Discontinuous SpanSet support is pooled only over covered token ranges; truncation yields partial coverage or Missing, never fabricated completeness. Any use in hierarchy induction triggers the existing anti-circularity ledger.

Please add a dependency diagram, the d_prop versus d_sem split, these grakern laws, and late-pooling coverage semantics to ADR 0001. With those additions I have no objection to you writing the ADR and spike plan. I will review both adversarially before any source bead opens.
